intervals.label: construction (detailed proposal to completed detector structures)
intervals.note: Start is the date of the official detailed proposal (August 1991), the earliest dated entry on the collaboration's own timeline; the timeline gives no start date for construction itself (the CTF prototype ran 1994-1996). The end is the year the timeline gives for completion of the detector structures.
intervals.quote: Official detailed proposal: August 1991 ... Detector structures construction completed in 2004

intervals.label: data taking
intervals.note: Start is the first DAQ run (detector filling was completed the day before, 15 May 2007); end is the last DAQ run, per the collaboration's own timeline.
intervals.quote: First DAQ run started on May 16, 2007 ... Last DAQ run (#36744) stopped on Oct 7, 2021

intervals.label: shut down
intervals.note: Terminal event: the last DAQ run, which the collaboration timeline dates to 7 October 2021.
intervals.quote: Last DAQ run (#36744) stopped on Oct 7, 2021

quantity.note: 278 t is the target (active) liquid-scintillator mass stated in the Extended Data Fig. 1 caption of the 2014 Nature pp-neutrino paper. The nominal fiducial mass is recorded separately on detector:borexino (specs.fiducial_mass); the pp analysis itself used a 75.5 t fiducial cut.
quantity.quote: The buffer and target scintillator masses are 889 and 278 t, respectively.

quantity.note: The Borexino collaboration's muon-flux paper places Borexino at 3800 m water-equivalent depth (its abstract gives 3800 m w.e. for the Gran Sasso laboratory). This differs from the ~1400 m rock / average LNGS overburden figure recorded on site:lngs-hall-c because m.w.e. and rock-metres are different units and per-hall shielding can differ from the site average.
quantity.quote: Cosmic-muon flux and annual modulation in Borexino at 3800 m water-equivalent depth

website.note: The certificate-mismatched domain borexino.lngs.infn.it redirects to/matches borex.lngs.infn.it; the latter is recorded as the working URL (checked 2026-09-17).

physics_goals.quote: It was designed to reveal low energy (sub-MeV) neutrinos in real time. Its main goals were to perform solar neutrinos spectroscopy and to measure the 7Be neutrino flux from the Sun.
physics_goals.value: Detect low-energy (sub-MeV) neutrinos in real time to perform solar-neutrino spectroscopy, including measurement of the 7Be neutrino flux from the Sun

summary.plain: A giant ball of ultra-pure liquid deep under the Gran Sasso mountain in Italy that directly watched low-energy neutrinos streaming from the Sun's core, including two kinds no one had ever seen before.
summary.technical: Liquid-scintillator (pseudocumene+PPO) solar-neutrino detector at LNGS Hall C, 278 t active mass (~100 t fiducial); detector structures completed in 2004, took data from 16 May 2007 to 7 October 2021. First direct spectral measurement of pp-chain neutrinos (2014) and first experimental evidence of CNO-cycle solar neutrinos (2020).

unique_capabilities.quote: the unprecedentedly radio-pure large-volume liquid-scintillator Borexino detector located at the underground Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso in Italy
unique_capabilities.value: Unprecedentedly radio-pure, large-volume liquid-scintillator detector able to see the CNO-cycle neutrino signal for the first time
